messages:
ashley: Heads up — new GPU node boots in eu-west-1 are failing since 03:17 UTC. Warmpool reports ~120 boot failures. Error in cloud-init: KMS decrypt timeout.

ops-bot: alert: gpu-provisioning-euw1 03:18 — 120 failures detected, error=KMSDecryptError, severity=high :rotating_light:

matt: logs? which subnet/route table?

ashley: quick tail from one init:```
2024-05-29T03:17:12Z node-init: KMSDecryptError: timed out contacting kms endpoint (endpoint=https://kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com)
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 30001 milliseconds
/etc/cloud-init/cloud.cfg.d/99-warm-config: failed to decrypt bootstrap secret
```

jia: rolled out a small egress tighten earlier at 02:50 UTC to the gpu-warmpool subnets (tagged: warmpool:euw1). I replaced the 0.0.0.0/0 route in rtb-0f1a2b with a route to nat-legacy (nat-0abc) to force traffic through the new NAT cluster.

matt: did that NAT have the right Elastic IP range? KMS caller-policy only allows our corporate egress IPs now, right?

samir: there's an additional twist — the VPC is attached to a transit gateway with peering propagation. We also propagated a route to the TGW earlier (for internal cross-region sync). Some traffic is leaking to an older NAT in a different account that uses a different EIP.

kelsey: confirming: recent IAM boundary update (PR #1624) added a condition that denies kms:Decrypt unless the request originates from our corporate IP block (203.0.113.0/24). That was to lock down accidental egress from dev subnets.

ashley: so nodes are egressing via nat-legacy which carries an EIP not in 203.0.113.0/24 -> KMS denies Decrypt -> boot fails. Makes sense.

matt: can we patch quickly by creating an interface VPC endpoint for KMS in the VPC? That would avoid egress entirely.

samir: yup, creating an interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.eu-west-1.kms) + security group that allows TLS from the GPU subnets will fix it without touching IAM policies. Quick plan: create endpoint, attach ENIs in subnets, update route (if needed), then retire nat-legacy routing.

ashley: alternative short rollback is to restore 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT that uses the corporate EIP, but that might take longer to roll through propagation.

kelsey: interface endpoint is safest. We should also tighten the endpoint policy to only allow the node role. Endpoint policy example:```
{
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": "*",
    "Action": "kms:*",
    "Resource": "*",
    "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gpu-node-role"}}
  }]
}
```

matt: also FYI the IAM boundary snippet causing the block looks like:```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "NotIpAddress": {"aws:SourceIp": "203.0.113.0/24"}
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

jia: I'll open a small PR to create the interface endpoint in the warmpool stack and attach the SG. Pushing now.

deploy-bot: deployment started: infra/warmpool/add-kms-endpoint (diff 187) — creating VPCEndpoint com.amazonaws.eu-west-1.kms

samir: once endpoint is up, we need to ensure node init uses the regional endpoint (it should auto-resolve). Also add an explicit /etc/hosts override if DNS split-horizon causes issues.

ashley: temporary mitigation — I'm reassigning the warmpool fleet to existing healthy NAT that matches corporate EIP. Doing that now.

deploy-bot: infra/warmpool/add-kms-endpoint succeeded (5m). VPCEndpoint vpce-0a1b2c created.

ashley: canary booted 3 nodes successfully after endpoint creation and one retry. Logs show successful KMS decrypt.

ashley:```
2024-05-29T03:31:10Z node-init: KMSDecrypt: success
2024-05-29T03:31:11Z bootstrap: secrets loaded
```

kelsey: we'll follow up with a postmortem: action items: 1) add endpoint to warmpool by default 2) validate NAT EIP mapping in the deployment playbook 3) add e2e test that ensures kms:Decrypt works under egress policy.

matt: +1. Also add a networking check to detect conflicting route propagation to TGW.

ashley: opening ticket INFRA-4723 for follow-ups and tagging owners. Monitoring for 2 hours, will update. Thanks everyone :heart:
